title: Annotatio II NATIVITAS: Rupert’s Genesis gold/fire analogy — bread still bread, yet truly Christ
pass_a_gloss: Then in the Commentary on Genesis bk. 6 ch. 32 handed down in these words: How, he says, is the bread which is seen Christ? To this I say, how is any species of metal, e.g. gold or silver (note here nonetheless the similitude usual with the Brothers of the Augsburg Confession, especially of iron) fused and resolved by a strong fire, in truth both gold and also called and is fire? For the gold is seen and is what it was, and yet most truly is called and is fire, which it was not: Therefore so altogether the bread brought near or immersed in the terrible and ineffable mystery of Christ’s passion still seems to be bread, which it was, and yet in truth is Christ, which it was not.
pass_b_english: Genesis commentary (VI.32): how is visible bread Christ? Like gold in strong fire — still gold to sight, yet truly called and is fire.
So bread brought into Christ’s passion-mystery still seems bread, yet in truth is Christ — a similitude Augsburg brothers later use of iron.
source_text: Tum Commentario in Genesin Lib. 6. cap. 32. his verbis tradito: Quomodo, inquit, panis, qui videtur, est Christus? ad hæc inquam, quomodo qualibet metalli species v. g. aurum sive argentum (nota tamen hîc similitudinem Fratribus Augustanae confessionis usitatam, praecipuè de ferro) valido igni conflatum atque resolutum, re vera & aurum est, & ignis quoque dicitur & est? Etenim aurum videtur & est, quod erat, & tamen verissimè ignis dicitur & est, quod non erat: Idcirco sic omnino panis admotus vel immersus terribili atque ineffabili mysterio passionis Christi, adhuc panis videtur esse, quod erat, & tamen in veritate Christus est, quod non erat.
